pharm: Selective vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist that reduces renal cAMP, prevents aquaporin-2 insertion into the collecting-duct membrane, and produces free-water excretion (aquaresis) with rising serum sodium; in ADPKD it slows cyst growth and kidney function decline.
quick: ADPKD: start 60 mg/day (45 mg AM + 15 mg 8 h later), titrate to max 90+30 mg/day
May be taken with or without food; drink water to avoid thirst/dehydration
Avoid; can cause fetal harm (animal data)
Contraindicated in anuria; not effective once kidney failure advanced
Boxed warning - serious/fatal liver injury; contraindicated in significant liver impairment
ALT/AST/bilirubin before start, at 2 and 4 weeks, monthly x18 months, then q3 months; serum sodium and volume status
summary: Tolvaptan is a selective vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist. The Jynarque formulation slows kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and carries a boxed warning for serious, potentially fatal liver injury requiring intensive LFT monitoring under a REMS program. The Samsca formulation treats clinically significant hypervolemic and euvolemic hyponatremia and must be initiated/reinitiated in hospital with close monitoring to avoid too-rapid sodium correction and osmotic demyelination.
indications: Slowing of kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) (Jynarque)

Clinically significant hypervolemic and euvolemic hyponatremia (serum sodium <125 mEq/L, or less marked hyponatremia that is symptomatic and resistant to fluid restriction), including in heart failure and SIADH (Samsca)
Not indicated for urgent correction of hyponatremia or where urgent sodium raising is needed

dosage.d: 60 mg/day: 45 mg on waking + 15 mg 8 hours later
Increase to 60+30 mg/day, then 90+30 mg/day if tolerated
dosage.t: At least 1-week intervals between titrations; max 120 mg/day

dosage.d: 15 mg once daily, may increase to 30 mg then 60 mg once daily at >=24-hour intervals
dosage.n: Do not restrict fluids during first 24 hours; monitor sodium closely

admin: Initiate and reinitiate hyponatremia (Samsca) therapy in a hospital where serum sodium can be monitored closely
Obtain baseline ALT, AST and bilirubin before starting Jynarque; follow the boxed-warning monitoring schedule
For ADPKD, take the larger dose on waking and the second dose 8 hours later; ensure access to water
Avoid fluid restriction during the first 24 hours of hyponatremia treatment to limit overly rapid correction
Do not co-administer with strong CYP3A inhibitors; avoid grapefruit juice
Jynarque is dispensed only through the Tolvaptan/ADPKD REMS program
moa: Tolvaptan is a selective antagonist of the vasopressin V2 receptor, with affinity about 1.8 times that of native arginine vasopressin and far greater for V2 than V1a. Blocking vasopressin binding in the renal collecting duct lowers adenylate cyclase activity and intracellular cAMP, preventing aquaporin-2 vesicles from fusing with the apical membrane. The result is increased free-water excretion (aquaresis), reduced urine osmolality and rising serum sodium. In ADPKD, the reduction in cAMP inhibits vasopressin-driven cyst-cell proliferation and fluid secretion, slowing kidney volume growth and functional decline.

absolute: History, signs or symptoms of significant liver impairment or injury (excludes uncomplicated polycystic liver disease)
Inability to sense or respond to thirst
relative: Patients at risk of overly rapid sodium correction (osmotic demyelination)
monitor: ALT, AST and total bilirubin (boxed-warning schedule)
Signs of hepatic injury and dehydration

preg: Avoid in pregnancy. Tolvaptan can cause fetal harm based on animal reproduction studies; weigh risk versus benefit and advise on contraception where appropriate.
lact: There is no information on tolvaptan in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: Tolvaptan is contraindicated in anuria and is ineffective once advanced kidney failure removes the aquaretic substrate. No major dose adjustment for mild-to-moderate renal impairment, but it should not be used where urinary outflow obstruction is uncorrected.
hepatic: BOXED WARNING: tolvaptan can cause serious and potentially fatal liver injury, including acute liver failure requiring transplantation. It is contraindicated in patients with significant liver impairment or injury (excluding uncomplicated polycystic liver disease). Measure ALT, AST and bilirubin before initiation, at 2 and 4 weeks, then monthly for 18 months and every 3 months thereafter; stop promptly for laboratory abnormalities or symptoms of hepatic injury.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors - ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir (contraindicated; markedly increase tolvaptan levels)
Strong CYP3A inducers - rifampin (avoid; reduce tolvaptan exposure)
Other hypertonic saline or drugs that raise sodium (additive overcorrection risk)
Desmopressin and other V2-receptor agonists (antagonized; avoid)
moderate: Digoxin (tolvaptan increases digoxin levels - P-gp inhibition)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit juice (CYP3A inhibition).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatic risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum sodium frequently after initiation/up-titration to avoid overly rapid correction.

serious: Serious and potentially fatal liver injury (boxed)
Osmotic demyelination from too-rapid sodium correction
GI bleeding in cirrhotic portal hypertension
emergency: Signs of liver failure (jaundice, dark urine, RUQ pain)
Neurologic deterioration from osmotic demyelination (dysarthria, dysphagia, quadriparesis)

monitoring: ALT, AST, bilirubin before start, at 2 and 4 weeks, monthly for 18 months, then every 3 months
Serum sodium frequently after initiation and up-titration (avoid >8-12 mEq/L rise in 24 hours)
Volume status, weight and signs of dehydration
Symptoms of hepatic injury at each visit
counsel: Expect increased urination and thirst; drink water in response to thirst to avoid dehydration
Report fatigue, loss of appetite, nausea, right upper abdominal pain, dark urine, or yellowing of eyes/skin immediately (liver injury)
Do not take strong CYP3A-inhibiting medicines or grapefruit juice
For hyponatremia therapy, treatment starts in hospital and sodium will be checked frequently
Keep all scheduled blood tests; Jynarque requires enrollment in a REMS program
Tell your doctor about all medicines, including desmopressin
pk: Aquaresis begins within ~2-4 hours of an oral dose
Approximately 12 hours (terminal); effective t1/2 ~3 hours for the aquaretic effect
Aquaretic effect persists several hours; dosed once or twice daily
pearls: Boxed warning: serious, potentially fatal liver injury - rigorous ALT/AST/bilirubin monitoring and a REMS program for Jynarque (ADPKD)
Initiate/reinitiate the hyponatremia indication (Samsca) in hospital and do NOT correct sodium too quickly - osmotic demyelination syndrome can result
Avoid fluid restriction during the first 24 hours of hyponatremia treatment
Strong CYP3A inhibitors are contraindicated; avoid grapefruit; dose-reduce with moderate inhibitors
Anticipate marked thirst and polyuria; ensure free access to water to prevent dehydration
missed: If a dose is not taken at the scheduled time, take the next dose at its scheduled time; do not double up. Do not attempt to make up missed doses.
overdose: No specific antidote. Expect exaggerated pharmacologic effects: rising serum sodium, polyuria, thirst and dehydration/hypovolemia. Assess vital signs, electrolytes, ECG and fluid status; replace water and electrolytes until aquaresis abates. Dialysis is unlikely to help (>98% protein bound).
